summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for increased respiratory secretions and suspected pneumonia after transfer from an outside ICU. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, with sputum cultures confirming Pseudomonas and Klebsiella. Treatment was adjusted to IV Zosyn based on sensitivities, and oral vancomycin was added for C. diff prophylaxis. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. His condition stabilized with improved respiratory status and no fever. HIV testing showed a viral load of 101 copies/mL and a CD4 count of 106. Orthopedic evaluation revealed worsening right hip osteoarthritis and foot inversion due to deconditioning, with recommendations for physical therapy. He was discharged to extended care to complete his antibiotic course and continue rehabilitation.
